newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central banker urges "rational" stock trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central banker urges "rational" stock trade.

text.p: Taiwan central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong said on Monday he was upset by the stock market's big recent downturn and urged investors to be more rational in their trading.
"The stock market has fallen so much. I am upset," Sheu told lawmakers in parliament. "I hope investors can be more rational. I hope the market can stabilise."
Sheu pledged that the bank would take the economy's health into consideration in any further issues of negotiable certificates of deposit.
"We will not continue to blindly issue NCDs," Sheu said. "We will do it in consideration of overall economic conditions."

The central bank has made major daily NCD issues almost every day of the past two weeks, aiming to soak up some of the loose liquidity that many analysts said was a main force fuelling the stock market's dramatic rise.
Taiwan share prices plunged about three percent on Friday on news of a major disease outbreak that would hurt Taiwan's pork exports.

Prices recovered slightly on Saturday, then tumbled 3.49 on Monday as an unconfirmed news report that rival China planned new war games in April triggered heavy profit-taking against the market's huge recent gains.

Brokers said they expected the downtrend to continue in the near term on heavy profit-taking pressure following months of dramatic gains that had lifted the index to a six-year high of 8,526.20 on March 18 -- a 23 percent rise in 1997 alone.
Even after Monday's plunge, the index was still a net 16.5 percent higher for 1997.
